sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house fast in Gates, New York?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house as it is. Gates is a town in Monroe County and a suburb of Rochester, so the town hall, the Monroe County Clerk and the county's tax portal handle most of the paperwork.

A fast sale mostly depends on having clean records. In Gates that means a current Compliance Certificate for any work done, a tax payoff figure and the right school district named on the bill.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Gates homes?
sections.html:
Gates is a mostly owner-occupied suburb of Rochester with a median home value of $170,500.

About 91% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which points to a settled community. Owners who have stayed that long may be selling a house with original systems, so a pre-listing walk-through can show what a buyer's inspector will raise.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about work and commuting in Gates?
sections.html:
Gates residents commute an average of 17.5 minutes, and 62.7% of people 16 and older are in the labor force. Some 92.3% of adults 25 and older finished high school and 28.5% hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

The town's economic base shows up in the 2022 receipts: transportation and warehousing at about $194 million, health care and social assistance at about $138 million, and retail sales at about $556 million. Those numbers sit alongside the Wegmans headquarters and Rochester Tech Park, both inside the town.

Median household income is $77,080, and about 11% of residents are in poverty. Ask your agent or lender how an appraisal could affect a financed buyer before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Where is Gates and how did it develop?
sections.html:
Gates sits in central Monroe County and borders the city of Rochester on its east side. It spans about 15.3 square miles, and the geographic center of Monroe County falls inside the town. Interstate 390 curves through the east, Interstate 490 crosses the middle, and Route 531 runs northwest toward Spencerport.

The area was organized in 1797 as Northampton in Ontario County. In 1808 the remaining portion was renamed Gates, after General Horatio Gates, and the town was incorporated on April 1, 1813. Monroe County was created in 1821. Parts of the old town later went to the city of Rochester and the Town of Greece.

  • Employers: Wegmans Food Markets keeps its headquarters in Gates, and Rochester Tech Park occupies a former Kodak plant site.
  • Zip codes: 14624 and 14606 cover most of the town, and a part falls under Spencerport's 14559.
  • Schools: the Gates-Chili and Spencerport school districts both draw on Gates property.

sections.h2: How did the 2025 reassessment change things for Gates sellers?
sections.html:
The Town of Gates states that it completed a town-wide reassessment in 2025, and the Assessor's page now lists a 2026 final tax assessment roll. For a seller, that means the assessed value printed on a tax bill is recent and tied to current market value.

The assessor's office compares each property to nearby sales and adjusts values when a building permit shows new construction, remodeling or demolition. The assessment funds the town, Monroe County, the school district and special district charges such as the fire and ambulance districts.

The assessment calendar runs on a fixed cycle:

  • March 1: taxable status date, and the exemption filing deadline.
  • May 1: tentative roll filed and grievance forms become available.
  • Fourth Tuesday in May: Grievance Day before the Board of Assessment Review, which has five resident members.
  • July 1: final roll filed, with decisions mailed by that date.

sections.h2: How are Gates property taxes billed and paid?
sections.html:
Gates owners receive two bills a year. The Town and County bill covers a calendar year and the school bill covers July 1 to June 30. The Tax Receiver's office is at 1605 Buffalo Road, and the town's page lists the interest schedule.

Because penalties rise month by month, a seller who is behind should get a written payoff figure before setting a closing date. After May 31, collection moves to the Monroe County Treasurer.

  • Town and County bill: mailed around the turn of the year, with full payment due by February 10 to avoid interest.
  • Late rates: interest begins at 1.5% from February 11 and climbs to 6% by May.
  • School bill: mailed so it arrives in early September, with full payment due by October 1.

sections.h2: Which town services and records are useful to a Gates seller?
sections.html:
The Town of Gates website carries most of the forms you may need while preparing a sale, and its Town Code is posted online. The Tax Receiver's office accepts cash, check and card, though a card payment adds a fee, and the town cautions that bill pay can take up to 14 days and arrive without a postmark.

  • Code complaints: the town accepts a code or dog complaint through an online form.
  • Electrical work: the town keeps a list of approved electrical inspectors, which helps if a buyer wants electrical work signed off.
  • Yard debris: a pickup schedule is posted online, and a refuse hauler list is available.
  • Fire and ambulance: special district charges for the Gates Fire Department and Gates Volunteer Ambulance are based on assessed value.

The Board of Assessment Review can only hear valuation complaints, not tax complaints, so a seller who thinks the bill is wrong should first check whether the assessed value or an exemption is at issue.

sections.h2: What permits and recording steps apply to a Gates sale?
sections.html:
The Gates Building Department reviews plans, issues permits for decks, pools, additions and signs, and issues Compliance Certificates. Zoning questions go to the same office, and a Zoning Compliance Request carries a $75 fee. The Zoning Board of Appeals meets the second Monday of each month for variance requests.

After closing, the deed is recorded by the Monroe County Clerk, who acts as registrar of deeds and mortgages, at 39 W. Main Street, Room 101 in Rochester. New York charges a seller's transfer tax of $2 per $500 of price, and the TP-584 form goes in with the deed. The Monroe County Real Property Portal shows tax bills and sales histories for parcels.

faqs.q: What is a Compliance Certificate in Gates?
faqs.a: It is a document the town Building Department issues after required permits and inspections are complete. Buyers' attorneys often ask for it when a seller added a deck, pool or alteration, so confirm yours is on file.

faqs.q: When is the Gates tax bill due without interest?
faqs.a: Full payment of the Town and County bill is due by February 10. Interest begins on February 11 at 1.5% and rises through May, and payments after May 31 go to the Monroe County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Gates house in?
faqs.a: Gates property falls within either the Gates-Chili Central School District or the Spencerport Central School District. Your tax bill names the district, and the Assessor's Office can confirm it.

faqs.q: Can I challenge my Gates assessment after the 2025 reassessment?
faqs.a: Yes. File the grievance form with the Assessor by the fourth Tuesday in May, and the Board of Assessment Review decides by July 1. Bring sales of similar nearby homes as evidence.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded for a Gates house?
faqs.a: At the Monroe County Clerk's office in downtown Rochester, which keeps deeds, mortgages and liens. The office is open weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
